agree.reason: The repeated '6 to 8 weeks' since June and the modest offers (a stair list, weekday meetings) make it hard to dismiss, but the letter leaves out its strongest facts, the missed dialysis appointments and the 74-of-112 majority, so a skeptical manager can still file it as a complaint.

honest.reason: The numbers match the brief, and the letter honestly concedes both the inspection and that a second elevator may not be possible, though 'more than five months later' and 'one day in every eight' depend on a current date the brief does not give.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns 41 days into a rate and points out the repeated estimate, but it never shows that 74 of 112 households is about two-thirds of the building, the figure that most directly answers the 'few loud people' view.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the status quo accurately: a second identical 6-to-8-week promise, a 12-day stretch and an inspection that does not measure reliability, so it shows that nothing will change unless management acts.

qualification.reason: It asks for a written response and a meeting but gives no deadline and says nothing about what happens if management doesn't respond, so the reader has nothing dated to check.

objections.reason: It meets the 'it passed inspection' and 'second elevator is impossible' objections well, but it leaves the reader's main dismissal, that this is a small loud minority, unanswered even though 74 of 112 households signed.

fit.reason: It has the right open-letter form at roughly 450 words, but the '[Management Company Name]' placeholder is left in the heading even though the company's name, Keystone Property Group, was available, and that looks unfinished for a letter going on the lobby wall and to the press.
